Iron Nutrition
Iron Deﬁciency
Iron deﬁciency is the most common nutrient deﬁciency, affecting as many as two-thirds of all children and women of child-bearing
age worldwide. It has been estimated that iron deﬁciency severe enough to cause anemia affects 20–25% of infants and as many as
40% of women and 25% of men. Iron deﬁciency occurs in industrially developed and developing countries. In the United States, 9–
11% of toddlers, adolescent girls, and women of child-bearing age have iron deﬁciency, and 2–4% have iron deﬁciency anemia. The
prevalence of iron deﬁciency is approximately doubled in US black and Hispanic women. The magnitude of this problem, however,
is related not only to the socio-economic status of the population studied, but also how iron deﬁciency and anemia are deﬁned (see
